findings.title: Public findMany method removed without migrating callers
findings.body: The conversion deletes InsightsBookingService.findMany, which previously accepted BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs and executed the query, and replaces it with getBaseConditions that only returns a Prisma.Sql fragment. No caller in this PR is updated to construct and execute a $queryRaw query instead. Any existing consumer calling service.findMany(...) will now fail TypeScript compilation (and would fail at runtime if untyped), breaking the insights data path until every call site is migrated.

findings.title: Event-type filter returns an unparenthesized OR expression
findings.body: buildFilterConditions stores the event-type condition as `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no parentheses around the whole OR, and when it is the only filter getFilterConditions returns that fragment unchanged. getBaseConditions happens to wrap it, but the public getFilterConditions result is unsafe to interpolate into a larger WHERE clause: `WHERE "userId" = 1 OR "eventParentId" = 2 AND <other>` is parsed by PostgreSQL as `"userId" = 1 OR ("eventParentId" = 2 AND <other>)` because AND binds tighter than OR, so rows can be returned that ignore the additional constraints. The previous structured Prisma where-object preserved this grouping automatically. The fragment should be wrapped as `((...) OR (...))` at construction.

findings.title: Multi-branch authorization conditions are not wrapped as a single expression
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition and buildTeamAuthorizationCondition reduce their branches to `(<branch A>) OR (<branch B>)` without enclosing the complete OR in parentheses, and the single-branch case returns a bare AND expression. getBaseConditions wraps the result, but the public getAuthorizationConditions result loses the grouping guarantee the old Prisma where-object provided: a caller interpolating it as `WHERE ${auth} AND <date/status condition>` gets `branchA OR (branchB AND <condition>)`, so branch A rows bypass the caller's date/status restrictions. This is an authorization-adjacent correctness risk; the builders should return a fully parenthesized expression.

findings.title: Org and team raw SQL is never actually executed against the database
findings.body: The org/team authorization tests only compare the returned Prisma.Sql object with an expected Prisma.Sql built from the same template syntax, and the sole $queryRaw execution test at line 481 exercises only the user scope. Consequently invalid PostgreSQL produced for org/team scopes — for example the `= ANY(${array})` parameter binding on lines 333-343 of the test / in the service, quoted identifiers, or boolean comparisons — would pass these tests and only fail (or misbehave) when a real org/team insights query runs. At least one org-scope and one team-scope test should execute the conditions via $queryRaw against the seeded data and assert the returned booking ids, especially since the PR description states the tests were not successfully run during development.

findings.title: Caching coverage deleted while caching logic remains
findings.body: This PR removes the entire 'Caching' describe block that verified repeated getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions calls return cached results, but the service still implements that caching (cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions in insightsBooking.ts). No replacement test covers it, so a regression that removes or breaks the cache — causing repeated membership/team database lookups on every insights query — would go undetected. The caching tests should have been ported to Prisma.Sql expectations like the other tests instead of deleted.
